title: A Verdict for the Parish
premise: Retired detective Ulyana Eriksen has traded homicide files for alphabetized shelves at her failing bookshop in the coastal parish of Marrow's End. A nervous stranger pays her a month's rent to prove that a murder scheduled for the parish trial of local teacher Elias Vane hasn't happened yet — and when the victim turns up dead exactly as predicted, Ulyana realizes the killer is using the original case file, the one she closed three years ago, as a script. As the trial clock ticks down, she must decode the killer's pattern, confront the wrongful conviction she helped secure, and lay a trap using the file itself. In the end she exposes the true murderer — the court clerk who transcribed every page — and chooses to stay in Marrow's End not as its detective but as one of its own.
about_author: Wendell Coldharbour is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade listening to verdicts from the back benches before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about places that remember too much and people who remember selectively.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the day she considers selling the bookshop, a hooded client leaves an envelope of cash and a single typed page: 'Prove the murder on March 14th does not happen.' She refuses, then finds the payment non-refundable and the page matches police stationery. The beat is wary curiosity — the hook of a puzzle she didn't ask for.

chapters.title: The File That Wouldn't Close
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She digs out her old case notes on the Vane conviction and finds pages subtly altered — dates shifted, a witness name inked over. Her former partner, DI Sorrel, dismisses her concerns as retirement restlessness. The emotional beat is professional pride curdling into dread: someone has been inside her past.

chapters.title: March the Fourteenth
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The predicted date arrives; nothing happens, and she almost laughs at herself — until the church organist is found drowned in the vestry, staged exactly like the three-year-old murder. The beat is cold shock: prophecy fulfilled, and she was meant to watch it happen.

chapters.title: A Town of Alibis
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with organist's widow, Maren. Ulyana interviews parishioners whose stories echo testimony from the old trial word for word. Maren reveals her husband had been receiving anonymous transcripts of the Vane proceedings. The beat is claustrophobia — the whole town reciting a script it doesn't know it's reading.

chapters.title: The Client Returns
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She traces the advance payment to a shell account and confronts the stranger: Elias Vane himself, released pending retrial, who hired her because he received the same prediction — dated before his release was approved. The beat is uneasy alliance; the man she helped convict may be her only honest ally.

chapters.title: Ink and Testimony
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. The official investigation stalls while Ulyana works parallel, comparing trial transcripts against the crime scene staging. She discovers every discrepancy maps to clerical annotations — marginalia only the person who typed the records could know. The beat is the thrill of the hunt sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Forgot
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A memory surfaces: the night of the original verdict, she noticed the clerk, Ambrose Pell, smiling at the guilty count — and said nothing. Guilt reframes her three years of hiding in the bookshop as penance. The beat is reckoning: her belonging in this town was built on a silence.

chapters.title: The Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A new typed page appears in her shop's returns bin: Vane will die before the retrial opens. Pell, sensing pursuit, accelerates — he needs the original verdict to stand so his transcription errors never surface. The beat is escalating urgency with a deadline now measured in days.

chapters.title: Staging the Verdict
chapters.summary: Ulyana, Vane, and Sorrel set their trap: they leak a false transcript containing a deliberate error only Pell would correct, then stage the courthouse archive as if the flawed original still exists. Pell takes the bait after hours. The beat is taut suspense — the hunter caught inside his own case file.

chapters.title: A Verdict for the Parish
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Pell confesses in the empty courtroom, insisting he merely corrected history. At the retrial, Vane is freed and Ulyana testifies to her own failure, finally filing the truth instead of hiding it. She reopens the bookshop with Maren as partner. The beat is quiet resolution: belonging earned by telling the truth.
